newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian parliament votes amnesty for Chechens.
newsitem.headline: Russian parliament votes amnesty for Chechens.

text.p: The Russian parliament voted overwhelmingly on Friday to approve an amnesty for Chechens and others who took part in the region's 21-month secessionist war against Russian forces.

The State Duma lower house, dominated by President Boris Yeltsin's communist opponents, backed the amnesty by 235 votes to 39. The instrument was proposed by a number of opposition-led committees. It aims to win the release of Russian prisoners-of-war by exchanging them for Chechens in detention.

The house voted by 228 to nil for a second, related motion giving the presidential committee responsible for prisoner exchanges carte blanche to release Chechens from Russian prisons in cases where this would win the freedom of captive Russians.

There are no accurate figures, but each side in the conflict says the other is holding hundreds, perhaps thousands, of its people. Their exchange, agreed as part of last August's ceasefire, is one of the most contentious issues in continuing peace negotiations.
Moscow accuses the Chechens of seeking freedom for common criminals. The Chechen separatists accuse Russia of classifying its guerrilla fighters as criminals in Russian jails.

Confusing the issue is the fact that considerable numbers of Russian servicemen still in Chechnya following the withdrawal of all remaining troops in January are accused by the Russian military authorities of being fugitive deserters.
